Either implement these members or keep the previous concrete DetectorHandler with an `evaluate` that returns `{}` until the stateful implementation is ready.
MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now an abstract subclass with no implementation, so it cannot be instantiated. This is an existing finding that still stands.

issues.descricao: The TODO above MetricAlertDetectorHandler says it will become a stateful detector, but the class already subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler.

comentarios.texto: The comment 'TODO: This will be a stateful detector when we build that abstraction' is now stale. MetricAlertDetectorHandler already subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler. Remove or reword the TODO.

Remove or revise the adjacent TODO saying this will become a stateful detector 'when we build that abstraction'. The class now inherits StatefulDetectorHandler, so the comment describes already-completed work as a future migration and misleads maintainers about which abstraction this handler uses.

issues.descricao: MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing its abstract methods, so instantiating it for metric alert detectors raises TypeError where it previously returned an empty-result handler.
issues.textoGolden: MetricAlertDetectorHandler inherits from StatefulDetectorHandler but only contains pass, failing to implement its required abstract methods: counter_names (property), get_dedupe_value(), get_group_key_values(), and build_occurrence_and_event_data(). This will cause a TypeError at runtime when the class is instantiated.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler with an empty body, so it does not implement the abstract methods counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data declared on StatefulDetectorHandler. WHY: the class is now abstract, and Detector.detector_handler (src/sentry/workflow_engine/models/detector.py:86) instantiates it via group_type.detector_handler(self), so any detector whose type resolves to this grouptype will raise TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler — the previous version implemented evaluate and was instantiable. HOW: implement the required abstract methods (or keep a concrete evaluate override) so the handler can be constructed.

MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but with `pass`, so it implements none of the abstract methods it inherits (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and the newly added build_occurrence_and_event_data). The class is therefore still abstract and instantiating it (it is registered as `detector_handler` on MetricAlertFire and is constructed by Detector.detector_handler) raises `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler with abstract methods ...`. Before this change it subclassed DetectorHandler and implemented the single abstract `evaluate`, so it was instantiable; the PR makes the metric-alert handler path throw. Either implement the required abstract methods or keep the class free of unimplemented abstracts.

MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler (an abc.ABC) with only `pass`. StatefulDetectorHandler declares four abstract methods — counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and the newly added build_occurrence_and_event_data (detector.py:142-170) — none of which are implemented here. The class therefore remains abstract and cannot be instantiated; Detector.detector_handler's `group_type.detector_handler(self)` will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler` for the metric_alert_fire group type. Previously this class was a concrete DetectorHandler with an implemented evaluate, so this PR newly makes it uninstantiable. Implement the required abstract methods (or revert to a concrete handler) to satisfy the base-class contract.

issues.descricao: The evaluate() docstring says it returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult, but it now returns a dict keyed by group key.
issues.textoGolden: Docstring says this returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult, but the method now returns a dict keyed by DetectorGroupKey. Consider updating the docstring to match the new return type.

comentarios.texto: Update evaluate's adjacent docstring to describe a dictionary keyed by DetectorGroupKey rather than a list of DetectorEvaluationResult. This change returns a dictionary and callers now consume .values(), but the documented return contract still tells readers to expect a list; iterating the documented result as a list would instead yield group keys.
Docstring says 'returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult' but signature/body now return dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]. Update docstring to describe dict keyed by group_key.

The evaluate() docstring still says it returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`. The method now returns a dict mapping group key to `DetectorEvaluationResult`. Update the docstring to describe the dict return shape.

issues.descricao: The mock occurrence builder ignores its value argument, so tests (e.g. group_2 expected with 6 while the packet carries 10) pass regardless of which value is passed to build_occurrence_and_event_data.
issues.textoGolden: Wrong value `6` passed for `group_2` occurrence — the data packet specifies `"group_2": 10`. Should be `10` to accurately reflect the test scenario, which will ensure the test produces the correct occurrence data.

comentarios.texto: The new occurrence builder accepts `value` but never incorporates or asserts it, so the occurrence tests cannot detect incorrect forwarding of the measured value to `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. For example, `test_state_results_multi_group` supplies 10 for group_2 but builds its expected occurrence with 6 and still passes. A regression that passes a constant or another group's measurement at the new production hook would therefore go unnoticed. Include the value in the mock occurrence's evidence and use the actual expected measurement, or assert the hook's arguments directly.

`build_mock_occurrence_and_event` accepts `value: int` but never uses it (the occurrence is built only from `group_key`/`new_status`), and this same helper is also the implementation of `MockDetectorStateHandler.build_occurrence_and_event_data`. Because neither the expected occurrence nor the handler output depends on the value, tests like `test_state_results_multi_group` (which incorrectly builds the group_2 occurrence with `value=6` while the packet carries `10`) and `TestEvaluate.test_dedupe` (expected built with 6 vs packet 8) pass regardless of the value actually passed into `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. If evaluation passed a wrong value, these tests would still pass, so they do not verify the value/threshold path they appear to cover. Include `value` in a field of the occurrence (or assert on it in the handler) and fix the wrong expected values so the argument is actually checked.

`build_mock_occurrence_and_event` accepts a `value: int` parameter but never uses it — the returned IssueOccurrence is derived only from `group_key` and `new_status`. Because `value` is dead, callers can pass a mismatched value with no failure: in `test_state_results_multi_group` the packet contains `group_2: 10`, but the expected occurrence for `group_2` is built with `6`. Either use `value` when constructing the occurrence so the test validates the group value, or drop the unused parameter and pass the correct value; otherwise the test silently accepts wrong group values.

sugestoes.texto: userPermDenialCacheKey joins name and parent with '_', and Grafana UIDs can contain '_'. For example, name="a"/parent="b_c" and name="a_b"/parent="c" both produce `..._a_b_c`. A cached denial for one resource then makes Check return Allowed:false for a different resource the user can access, for up to shortCacheTTL. Fix: use a separator that cannot appear in UIDs, or prefix each segment with its length.

If the cached permission map exists but does not allow the resource, Check always calls getIdentityPermissions. getUserPermissions no longer has a cache short-circuit, so this runs a full GetUserPermissions DB query (and rewrites permCache) for every distinct (user, action, name, folder) that is denied. Checking many items the user cannot access (for example, filtering search results) now costs one DB query per item where it used to be one cached map. Singleflight only merges concurrent identical calls and the denial cache only helps on repeats, so consider rate-limiting the refresh, for example by refetching at most once per user/action per short interval.

issues.descricao: The denial cache key joins name and parent folder with underscores, so different name/parent pairs can collide and a cached denial for one resource denies another until TTL expiry.
issues.textoGolden: The cache key construction in `userPermDenialCacheKey` uses simple string concatenation with underscores, which can lead to ambiguous keys and collision risks when any component contains underscores or is empty. This could result in incorrect denial cache hits, affecting user permissions.

comentarios.texto: The denial cache key does not distinguish underscores inside resource and parent UIDs from its field separators. For the same namespace, user and action, (name="a_b", parent="c") and (name="a", parent="b_c") generate the same key, so denying the first request makes Check return false for the second even if its permissions explicitly allow it. Encode the components unambiguously, for example as a JSON tuple or length-prefixed fields.

The denial cache key is not injective: for the same namespace, user and action, `(name="a_b", parent="c")` and `(name="a", parent="b_c")` produce the same key. After the first request stores a denial, Check's new early cache return denies the second request without checking its permissions, even if it is allowed. Encode the components unambiguously (for example a JSON tuple or length-prefixed components) and add a test verifying that these two requests do not share a denial entry.

Make the denial-cache key encode component boundaries unambiguously (for example, length-prefix or serialize the components). For the same namespace, user and action, name `a_b` with parent `c` and name `a` with parent `b_c` both produce the suffix `_a_b_c`. Underscores can occur in resource UIDs, so denying the first request caches a key that causes Check to immediately deny the second request without evaluating its permissions, even if that resource is allowed.

issues.descricao: The explicit denial-cache test seeds the cached permission as false instead of true, so it would pass without the denial-cache short-circuit and does not verify it.
issues.textoGolden: The test comment says the cached permissions 'allow access', but the map stores false for dashboards:uid:dash1, so checkPermission will still treat this scope as not allowed.

comentarios.texto: This test claims to prove the permDenialCache short-circuit (service.go:116-121) denies access, but it seeds the cached permission as map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false} (a deny), contradicting its comment "Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked". Because the cached set is already a deny, checkPermission returns allowed=false, the code falls through to the DB path, and the fake store also returns no permissions, so Allowed stays false. The assertion passes even if the entire permDenialCache early-return were deleted. Seed the cached permission as true (map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": true}) so that only the denial-cache entry can force Allowed=false; otherwise the test does not verify the feature.

The comment says "Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked", but the code sets the permCache entry to `false`, which is a deny. The test therefore does not show that the permission cache is skipped. Set the value to `true`, or change the comment to match.

The 'Should deny on explicit cache deny entry' test would still pass if the permDenialCache check were removed. permCache is seeded with dash1:false, not true as the comment claims, so the normal path also denies. Seed permCache with {"dashboards:uid:dash1": true} and a store that grants the permission, so Allowed=false can only come from the denial entry.

issues.descricao: A cached permission set that denies a resource always triggers a full DB permission reload, so checks over many inaccessible dashboards issue one query per resource instead of being served from cache.

comentarios.texto: Every distinct resource denied by the cached permission map triggers a reload of the entire user's action permission set, because the denial cache is resource-specific and a cached false result always falls through to getIdentityPermissions. Sequential checks of N inaccessible dashboards therefore execute N full permission queries and cache rewrites even with a current action-wide cache; getUserPermissions' singleflight only merges overlapping requests. Bound refreshes per user/action with a short refresh cooldown or generation marker so different resource misses can share a recent refresh.

issues.descricao: The Service struct comment listing its caches was not updated for the new permDenialCache field.

comentarios.texto: The struct doc comment still reads "// Cache for user permissions, user team memberships and user basic roles", but this PR added the new `permDenialCache` field (line 58). The comment no longer enumerates what the struct actually holds and misleads a reader about the new denial-cache field; update it to mention the permission-denial cache so the prose matches the fields.

sugestoes.texto: Each `import()` is written directly as an object-literal value, so all app modules start loading as soon as `@calcom/app-store` is imported, and the async conversion adds await overhead without deferring anything. Any caller of getCalendar, getVideoAdapters or the payment lookups still pulls in every app's dependencies (Google, Office365, Stripe, etc.) at module load. To make the loading lazy, wrap each entry in a thunk, e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`, and call it at the use sites (`await appStore[key]?.()`).

Making the `forEach` callback `async` and awaiting `getCalendar` inside it moves any error from `getCalendar` (such as the CalendarService constructor throwing) out of the surrounding `try/catch`. That error is now an unhandled promise rejection instead of being logged, which can crash the Node process or trigger unhandled-rejection handlers. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => { ... }))` inside the try block so failures are caught.

The `async` `forEach` callback awaits `getCalendar`, so its rejections bypass the enclosing `try/catch` and become unhandled promise rejections instead of being logged. Before this PR, a synchronous throw from getCalendar was caught here. Replace it with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` inside the try block.

The `async` `forEach` callback that now awaits `getCalendar` is fire-and-forget, so a rejection from getCalendar is an unhandled promise rejection instead of an error the tRPC mutation can surface. The request also returns before the calendar deletions have been attempted. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => ...))`.

issues.descricao: Async callbacks passed to forEach after getCalendar became async are never awaited, so calendar and video cancellations run fire-and-forget, may not finish, and their errors escape the surrounding try/catch as unhandled rejections.
issues.textoGolden: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.

comentarios.texto: The async forEach callback moves calendar factory exceptions outside the surrounding try/catch because forEach discards its returned promise. An invalid encrypted Exchange credential throws during CalendarService construction, now producing an unhandled rejection while Reschedule continues and returns success instead of logging the error; the identical regression occurs in wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts. Await Promise.all over bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...) inside the try block, or use an awaited for...of loop, so factory and deletion failures reach the catch.

The new async forEach callback is not awaited. If getCalendar rejects (for example, the dynamically imported calendar module fails to load or its service constructor throws), the callback produces a rejected promise that forEach discards; the surrounding try/catch cannot catch it. Previously a synchronous getCalendar failure reached that catch. Await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...)) or use an awaited for...of loop so these failures remain handled and calendar cleanup completes before rescheduling continues. Apply the same fix to the equivalent changed loop in wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts.

WHAT: credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { await getCalendar; apiDeletes.push(...) }) pushes to apiDeletes asynchronously after outer code consumes it. WHY: outer apiDeletes is awaited elsewhere while async callbacks have not yet pushed, so recurring-event deletions are lost/partial and errors are unobserved. HOW: replace with for...of with await or collect promises via map + await Promise.all.

issues.descricao: Each import(...) in the appStore object literal runs when app-store/index.ts is imported, so all integrations still load at startup instead of lazily, while every entry becomes a promise.

sugestoes.texto: The constructor now takes `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`, where `teamId` is optional for every scope, instead of the discriminated union `InsightsBookingServiceOptions`, so `{ scope: "team" }` without `teamId` now compiles. The zod `safeParse` then fails, `this.options` becomes null, and the service silently returns `1=0`, giving empty insights instead of a compile-time error. Keep `options: InsightsBookingServiceOptions` in the constructor signature (or make the public type a discriminated union with `teamId` required for `scope: "team"`).

issues.descricao: In getBaseConditions, the branches for a missing authorization condition are unreachable because getAuthorizationConditions always returns a Prisma.Sql.
issues.textoGolden: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

comentarios.texto: getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql, so the `else if (filterConditions)` and final `else` branches (returning NOTHING_CONDITION) in getBaseConditions can never execute. Simplify to: if filterConditions, combine it with authConditions; otherwise return authConditions.

Unreachable branches in getBaseConditions: authConditions is always a truthy Prisma.Sql object (never null, NOTHING is `1=0`), so `else if (filterConditions)` and final `else { return NOTHING }` can never execute. Simplify to if(filter) return auth AND filter else return auth, or make the nothing-case explicit.

WHAT: `getBaseConditions` returns `filterConditions` alone (no authorization predicate) when `authConditions` is falsy (`else if (filterConditions) { return filterConditions; }`). WHY: The WHERE clause returned to consumers then contains no ownership/authorization restriction, so a caller using it would return every booking matching the filters (e.g. all bookings for the given eventTypeId/memberUserId) regardless of the requesting user's org/team membership — an authorization-boundary bypass if `getAuthorizationConditions()` ever yields a falsy value. HOW: Always AND the authorization predicate with the filters and fall back to `NOTHING_CONDITION` when no auth predicate exists, e.g. `return filterConditions ? Prisma.sql`(${authConditions}) AND (${filterConditions})` : authConditions;` (or keep the `NOTHING_CONDITION` default when auth is missing).

issues.descricao: The getBaseConditions test uses a single booking matching both auth and filter conditions, so it would pass even if the conditions were not combined.

comentarios.texto: The rewritten "should combine authorization and filter conditions" test cannot fail if the combination is broken. The fixture creates a single booking that satisfies the auth condition (userId = user.id AND teamId IS NULL) and the filter condition (eventTypeId = eventType.id) independently, so getBaseConditions returning auth-only, filter-only, or the AND combination all yield the same single-row result asserted here. Only a `1=0` result would be caught. Make the data distinguish the two: add a booking that matches the filter but not the auth (e.g. a team booking with the same eventTypeId), then assert the result excludes it, so that dropping either branch changes the returned rows.

issues.descricao: The caching tests for getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions were removed in the Prisma.sql conversion, leaving the cached-condition logic untested.
Claims getBaseConditions returns OR fragments without parentheses, so a caller appending `AND <extra>` would leak rows outside the authorization scope.
The new public options type makes teamId optional for team scope, so a missing teamId compiles and silently yields empty insights instead of a type error.

sugestoes.texto: The fallback locales (site default and :en) are only loaded by FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!, and the only caller is ApplicationController#set_locale. Lazy loading in I18n.translate (translate_accelerator.rb:68) loads only config.locale. As a result, translations in Sidekiq jobs, mailers, rake tasks or I18n.with_locale blocks can try fallbacks whose locale files were never loaded and return 'translation missing'. Fix: in the patched I18n.translate, load every locale in I18n.fallbacks[config.locale] instead of only config.locale, for example by calling I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! there.

The fallback chain now depends on SiteSetting.default_locale. However, the translate_accelerator LRU cache key (`#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}`) does not include the default locale. After an admin changes the default locale, users whose strings fell back to the old site locale keep getting the old cached text. Fix: add SiteSetting.default_locale to the cache key, or clear the I18n cache when default_locale changes.

issues.descricao: Fallback locale catalogs are only loaded in the controller's set_locale filter, while translate loads just the current locale, so translations outside requests (jobs, mailers) cannot fall back to the site default or English.

comentarios.texto: Fallback catalogs are ensured loaded only in the controller filter, leaving non-controller translation paths without the catalogs required by the newly enabled fallback backend. Jobs::Base sets I18n.locale directly and PostAlerter uses I18n.with_locale, while the accelerator loads only the current locale and backend fallback lookups bypass that loader; missing keys therefore still produce missing translations or skip the configured site fallback until another request happens to load those catalogs. Ensure the full fallback chain is loaded at the translation boundary, rather than relying solely on the controller filter.

The new fallbacks contract requires the fallback locales (site default and :en, from FallbackLocaleList#[]) to be loaded before Backend::Simple#translate is asked for them — Backend::Simple only returns already-loaded translations. This PR added I18n.ensure_loaded!/I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! but wired it only into ApplicationController#set_locale, and the loader that actually gates every translation, I18n.translate (line 68), still loads only `config.locale`. As a result, any I18n.t performed outside the request cycle (console, background jobs, mailers) or before set_locale runs will not load the fallback locales and will silently return 'translation missing' instead of the fallback the new I18n.fallbacks advertises. Fix: have translate ensure the fallback chain is loaded (e.g. call I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! / load the fallback locales here), not rely on the controller hook.

translate loads only config.locale, but the new fallback chain (default_locale, :en) is loaded only by the controller's I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!. Outside controllers (jobs, mailers, rake), a key missing in the current locale falls back to a locale that is not loaded, so it returns 'translation missing', and the LRU cache then stores that result. Fix: in translate, call I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! (or load each locale in fallbacks[config.locale]) before the lookup.

issues.descricao: The translation cache key does not include the site or its default locale, but fallback results now depend on SiteSetting.default_locale, so multisite processes or a changed default locale serve stale fallback translations.

comentarios.texto: The new fallback order depends on SiteSetting.default_locale, but the accelerator's translation cache does not include that setting or the current site in its key. In a multisite process, two sites with the same user locale and different default locales reuse the first site's cached fallback translation; changing the default locale also leaves cached fallback results stale. Include the effective fallback chain or site/default-locale context in the translation cache key.

sugestoes.texto: After taking the write lock, the code never checks the cache again, so every goroutine that saw a nil cache under RLock will reload the assets one after another (file open, JSON decode, building the integrity map) even after the first one has filled the cache. When the cache is cold, concurrent requests queue on the exclusive lock and repeat the same blocking load. Fix: right after `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()`, add `if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }`.

issues.descricao: GetWebAssets does not re-check the cache after acquiring the write lock, so concurrent callers that missed the cache each reload the assets manifest.
issues.textoGolden: The GetWebAssets function implements an incomplete double-checked locking pattern for caching web assets. The function first checks if the cache is populated using a read lock (RLock), and if the cache is empty, it acquires a write lock to populate it. However, it fails to re-check whether the cache was populated by another goroutine while waiting to acquire the write lock.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: The exclusive lock acquired at line 48 is held (via defer on line 49) across the blocking file read / synchronous CDN HTTP request (lines 56-67) and there is no re-check of entryPointAssetsCache after acquiring the lock. WHY: On a cold cache, all concurrent callers (api/index.go:82, api/frontendsettings.go:62, middleware/recovery.go:141) block on the write lock and then each sequentially re-executes the full load (file I/O or blocking http.DefaultClient.Do), producing a thundering-herd serialization and N redundant loads instead of one; in Dev mode this happens on every request since the fast path is skipped, serializing all concurrent page loads. HOW: after `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()` re-check the cache (`if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }`) so only the first goroutine performs the load, and drop the defer in favor of releasing the lock immediately after assigning `entryPointAssetsCache = result` to avoid holding it during I/O.
cache is not re-checked under the lock after re-acquiring write Lock, so concurrent callers can each recompute web assets

The cache is not rechecked after acquiring the write lock, so concurrent production requests that initially observe a nil cache each reload and decode the manifest even after another request has populated it. During a cold-start request burst, these redundant filesystem reads and JSON decodes execute serially under the global lock, delaying queued page and frontend-settings requests and blocking cache readers while each reload runs. After acquiring the write lock, return the populated cache when cfg.Env != setting.Dev before performing asset loading.

issues.descricao: GetWebAssets holds a global exclusive mutex through the whole manifest load, so in Dev mode, where the cache is bypassed, every request serializes behind it.

sugestoes.texto: RunCommands and QueryFramesInto now always return 'not implemented', so sql.TablesList and NewSQLCommand always fail. This breaks the existing tests in pkg/expr/sql/parser_test.go (e.g. lines 12-212 expect parsed tables) and pkg/expr/sql_command_test.go:10 (expects NewSQLCommand to succeed), so CI will fail. Either remove or skip those tests, or rewrite them to expect the disabled-feature error.

enableSqlExpressions returns false on both branches, so the FlagSqlExpressions check is dead code and the feature can never be enabled through the flag. Anyone reading or maintaining it will think the flag controls SQL expressions when it does not. If the goal is to disable SQL expressions unconditionally, drop the flag lookup and return false with a comment. Otherwise return h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions).

comentarios.texto: After replacing `duck.NewInMemoryDB()` with local `NewInMemoryDB()` and removing the duck import, the local `duckDB` still carries the old implementation name though it is no longer a duck DB. Rename to `db`/`sqlDB` (as done in sql_command.go) so identifier matches code.

issues.descricao: enableSqlExpressions returns false on both branches, so ReadQuery rejects every SQL expression query as not implemented even when the sqlExpressions feature flag is enabled.
The variable `enabled` in enableSqlExpressions holds the negated flag value, so it is true when SQL expressions are disabled and the name states the opposite of its value.
NewInMemoryDB returns a stateless stub whose methods all return 'not implemented', so its name misleads callers expecting a working in-memory database.
